My suggestion on the reference implementation, after reading @enj 's comments is like so...

The GRPC server, which implements the `GRPC service interface` expects an implementation that satisfies `kms.Service interface`.

The local key logic can be a `kms.Service interface` middleware. So it expects a `kms.Service interface` it can fallback to, if it doesn't know a key or needs to encrypt its own local KEK.

So the local `kms.Service interface` implementation would be need to:
- have a storage of `value.Transformer`s
- have a reference to the current `value.Transformer` in use (if we put it into the cache, it might vanish)
- have a reference to another `kms.Service interface`, which should be the remote KMS.

So the sub-stories could look like:
- write Middleware
- write Transformers that can get exhausted (by time, by usage)
- write `value.Transformer`'s storage
- write some `kms.Service interface` dummy for remote KMS?

I have some sketches of what I am talking about [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114315#issuecomment-1353257179).

> * write some `kms.Service interface` dummy for remote KMS?

I would implement that in terms of the `crypto/cipher.Block` interface so that it can be used both in testing (via a local key) and in real code (by delegating to a HSM).

review_comments: `managedKeys` should have more control over the annotations.

Is this basically the same as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/91dbd82cdec4f608abe3f1217566b4d114c7879e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/value/encrypt/envelope/kmsv2/envelope.go#L52-L60 ?

The kms provider implementer would invoke `NewKeyManagementService` in the provider to initialize? If that's the case shouldn't we allow the implementer to configure the cache size with an options struct?
Since our state is currently loss on restart, isn't this basically the number of "restarts" we can hold in memory?

Well I would assume we would hold 99 of the most popular keys and one that is current, due to the LRU cache... well... actually... we might even loose the current one... TODO @ibihim.

In the worst case, when a KMS plugin was able to encrypt at least one file, it is used frequently and this times 99, we have a kms v1 solution.

If we have plenty of restarts due to misconfiguration, I would hope that no file gets encrypted.

We validate if annotation keys are fully qualified domain name https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f14ebac384ffd0a7adc09e5098b0c567042390a0/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/value/encrypt/envelope/kmsv2/envelope.go#L293, so this needs to be updated to a valid name
Could you add a comment to all the exported functions? (relevant for all the files in the PR)
Could you add more details in the comment about why a nonce is prepended?
Using `aes.NewGCMTransformer`, no reason to mention it any more 😄

I think we should attempt to re-use existing, related code (with refactors as needed) instead of writing net new things:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/91dbd82cdec4f608abe3f1217566b4d114c7879e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/encryptionconfig/config.go#L313

It definitely makes sense to reuse the code. What kind of prefix should we have?

1. `k8s:enc:aesgcm:v1` or something specific to the plugin like `kmsplugin:enc:aesgcm:v1`.
2. What kind of names are typically used for the `apiserverconfig.AESConfiguration` `keys`? What should we use for the plugin-KEKs?

Would it make sense to make an `AppendableTransformer` (fail-through) or even an `AppendablePrefixTransformer`?

All the transformers used  by `prefixTransformers`  are set on initialization. If one could append, it would be a perfect fit and replace quite a lot of code.
I need to think on what approach is best in regards to prefixing.  I have concerns around API stability and allocations on the hot path.
Ok, I will use the aesGCMTransformer with the LRU cache as of now. Then move away from LRU and use the expiring cache... and then we can revisit the prefixes.

Need to add the copyright header in all the files

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f14ebac384ffd0a7adc09e5098b0c567042390a0/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/value/encrypt/envelope/kmsv2/envelope.go#L1-L15
Is this how it should look like @enj?

Not a blocker for this but we're planning to move away from lru cache to use expiring cache in the kms v2 implementation (ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/111920). We'll need to revisit this and check if we want to use expiring cache in reference implementation too.
Lets have a shared implementation between kms v2 and the reference implementation.
